notes: South Carolina's All-State Chorus is run by the SCMEA Choral Division (choraldivision.org), a division of the South Carolina Music Educators Association. It is a high-school-only (grades 9-12) program with a single live audition round held over five days in November, followed by an All-State Chorus Weekend in February. The Choral Division also runs High School Region Choirs and Middle School Region Clinics, which are separate from All-State and not captured here. For 2026-27 the All-State Chorus Weekend is February 25-27, 2027 at Winthrop University, with the public concert February 27 at 3:00 p.m. The 2026-27 conductors/clinicians and performance repertoire had not been published at retrieval time.

organization.name: SCMEA Choral Division
organization.description: The Choral Division of the South Carolina Music Educators Association, whose stated purpose is 'providing leadership and assistance for the development of choral music programs.' It administers the All-State Chorus, Region Choirs, Concert Performance Assessment (CPA), and Solo & Ensemble.

programs.name: South Carolina All-State Chorus
programs.description: The SCMEA Choral Division All-State Chorus is composed of up to three ensembles chosen randomly from the highest-scoring students at a single statewide solo audition. Auditions are held November 3-7, 2026 at the Lexington 2 Performing Arts Center; the All-State Chorus Weekend is February 25-27, 2027 at Winthrop University, ending in a public concert on February 27 at 3:00 p.m. Membership is based on the total points received in the audition, out of a maximum composite score of 204.

dates.title: Audition registration forms and fees due
dates.description: Registration forms must be completed online and appropriate fees paid online or payment check postmarked by Thursday, October 1, 2026. Late and/or incomplete registrations will not be allowed to audition — no exceptions.

dates.title: All-State Chorus Auditions — Lexington 2 Performing Arts Center
dates.description: Solo auditions in two phases: prepared audition selection (blind) and sight-singing (blind). All students must audition at their school's assigned time.

dates.title: All-State Chorus Weekend registration fee due
dates.description: Registration forms completed online and fees paid online or payment check postmarked by Friday, December 11, 2026. Late payments result in a rule violation.

dates.title: Absence documentation due to the All-State Chorus Weekend Coordinator
dates.description: All written documentation pertaining to absences must be submitted two weeks prior to the All-State Chorus Weekend. Requests for exceptions due to extenuating circumstances must also be submitted in writing two weeks prior.

dates.title: All-State Chorus Weekend — Winthrop University, Rock Hill, SC
dates.description: A more detailed schedule will be provided when it is available. Attendance at 100% of the weekend is required.

requirements.title: Grades 9-12, enrolled for credit
requirements.description: Auditions are open to all singers in grades 9-12 who are enrolled in the director's program for credit. Students must be enrolled for at least one credit during the 26-27 school year in a school choral program.

requirements.title: Director must hold active NAfME membership and be in good standing with SCMEA
requirements.description: The school choral program must be directed by a member with an active NAfME membership and in good standing with SCMEA. Membership of the director is verified through the NAfME database. A director may not sponsor students enrolled in a school other than his/her own. Failure to comply results in the involved students being unable to participate in All-State Chorus Weekend and their school being suspended from auditions for the next academic year.

requirements.title: Home-schooled students
requirements.description: Home-schooled students enrolled in a public or home-school choral program for at least one credit in the 26-27 school year must provide documentation qualifying them as 9th-12th grade students and as a member of a South Carolina Home School Association at the time of registration.

requirements.title: Two-phase blind solo audition
requirements.description: Phase 1 — prepared audition selection, performed blind (students behind a curtain, screen, or partition, or judges seated with backs to students). Students perform their part along with a provided audition prompt track that includes the starting pitch for their voice part and the other four voices played by piano with their own part omitted throughout. Phase 2 — sight-singing, in the same room immediately afterward, also blind. After sight-singing, students leave the building and have no contact with students waiting to audition.

requirements.title: Prepared piece scoring
requirements.description: Each student auditions individually before three judges. Score range 0-50 from each judge, with up to ten points in each of: Rhythmic and Timing Accuracy, Pitch and Intonation, Diction, Tone Quality, Musicality. Maximum score for the prepared piece is 150 (50 points from three judges).

requirements.title: Sight-singing procedure
requirements.description: All directions are given from a recorded prompt. The example is 8 measures, printed on two lines of four measures each. Students are given the tonic triad and beginning pitch, have 60 seconds to practice, then hear the tonic triad and beginning pitch again and have 45 seconds to sing through the piece. Students set their own tempo; no count-off is given. They may sing on solfege, numbers, la, ta, count-singing, etc. Score range 0-18 per judge.

requirements.title: Sight-reading parameters
requirements.description: The piece will be in any major key. It will start on Do and end on Do. The most difficult rhythm will be a dotted quarter note followed by an eighth note. Skips will come from the I, IV, and V7 triads (Do-Mi-Sol; Fa-La-Do; Sol-Ti-Re-Fa). There may be quarter rests. Students receive 1 point for completing each half measure accurately (beats 1-2, beats 3-4), one point for retaining tonic, and one point for flow (steady tempo, no hesitations or restarts). Students must attempt the rhythmic pattern and melodic contour to receive points for retaining tonic and flow.

requirements.title: Maximum composite score 204
requirements.description: The maximum possible composite score is 204 — 150 from the prepared piece and 54 from sight-singing. Individual singers are selected according to total points. The All-State Chorus is composed of up to three ensembles chosen randomly from the highest-scoring students.

requirements.title: Alternates
requirements.description: After each audition cycle the committee examines cutoff scores per voice part and may appoint as Alternates students who missed the cutoff by one to three points; the exact range is decided year by year based on scoring spread. Alternates must register fully to be eligible, are assigned to an ensemble to prepare, participate in part checks, and are selected at random from their voice part as spots open. Alternates not called serve as invited auditors.

requirements.title: No digital devices at the audition site
requirements.description: Absolutely no digital devices — phones, smart watches, CD players/recorders, iPods, MP3 players, video/DVD recorders, radios, or text messaging devices — are allowed in or near the audition site. Cell phones must be off and left outside the building. A confiscated device forfeits the student's audition and gives the school a level 1 violation. Teachers and students must respect the confidentiality of the sight-singing process.

requirements.title: Teacher must be present; no photocopied music
requirements.description: Teachers must be present with their students at the auditions; students not accompanied by their own teacher will not be allowed to audition. No photocopied music is allowed (the only exception is a year in which the audition piece is out of print). No changing of clothes on site. Students who have previously been All-State members must audition again.

requirements.title: Music screening / part check
requirements.description: A music screening/part check event occurs at the beginning of the first rehearsal. Committee members walk through while the choir sings each piece to verify preparation. Singers who cannot demonstrate proficiency, are significantly late to a rehearsal, miss an entire rehearsal, or commit a major rule infraction become Auditors — they attend all rehearsals seated at the back and may attend guest performances and social activities, but may not sing in the concert.

requirements.title: 100% attendance required
requirements.description: All selected students must attend 100% of the All-State Chorus Weekend. Teachers and students must be present at all All-State Chorus activities, and teachers must stay at the same hotel as their students. Only participants, official chaperones (at least 21 years of age), and teachers may be present at hotels, rehearsals, or connected facilities; no children are allowed at any rehearsal.

requirements.title: Concert dress code
requirements.description: Permitted: black tuxedo/suit with white or black long-sleeved button-down shirt and black tie or bow tie (black vest optional); formal black button-down with full-length sleeves and lay-down collar, black tie/bow tie and black pants; black formal full-length concert dress; black dress past the knee with fully opaque black tights; black ankle-length skirt with black blouse; black full-length pants with dressy black blouse or jacket and blouse. Students wearing pants must wear black socks or hose and black dress shoes. Strictly prohibited: slits above the kneecap, bare midriff or back, spaghetti straps, cocktail or prom dresses, show choir attire, sneakers/sandals/slides, low-cut or revealing necklines, and heels/shoes higher than 2 inches. Attire is checked for compliance before the concert; non-compliant students are prohibited from singing.

requirements.title: Rehearsal requirements
requirements.description: Dress for rehearsals is informal regular school clothes; hats, sunglasses, or other interfering items are prohibited. No gum, talking, tobacco, vaping, or illegal substances. Each student must bring a pencil and their music to all rehearsals even if memorized, and will need a black folder for the concert. Rehearsal tracks are provided for each student.

repertoire.title: Honor and Glory
repertoire.notes: 2026-27 prepared audition selection. Audition tracks (starting pitch plus the other four voices on piano with the auditioning part omitted) are provided by the SCMEA Choral Division via Google Drive. Composer and editor credited exactly as listed by SCMEA.

fees.description: $20.00 per student, remitted to the All-State Chorus Chairperson with a digital submission of the Audition Request Form. Paid online at registration or by a single school check, personal check, or money order payable to SCMEA Choral Division. Non-refundable — once registration materials are submitted, no refunds, no substitutions of names, no voice part changes, and no other changes.
Non-refundable All-State Chorus Weekend registration fee of $55.00 per participating student, in addition to the audition fee. Due December 11, 2026.
